name: Biased Sampling for Path Depth
aliases: Biased Sampling for Path Depth — Density and Anisotropy Reduction with Ray Depth
Density and Anisotropy Reduction with Ray Depth
definition: A biasing technique that reduces medium density and anisotropy as the ray depth (bounce count) increases, resulting in larger sampled distances, fewer scattering events per path, reduced variance, and faster convergence at the cost of slight bias.
summary: Biased Sampling for Path Depth reduces variance in volumetric path tracing by exponentially decaying extinction and anisotropy with ray depth, trading negligible visual bias for massive performance gains.
